[DOCUMENTATION / 05]{.article-label}

Start with the system design. For bench work, read hardware integration and the bring-up sequence before calibration or control tuning. The detailed guides retain the repository’s engineering notes as their source of truth.

```{=html}
<div class="doc-grid">
<a class="doc-card" href="docs/design.html"><span class="article-label">01 / UNDERSTAND</span><h2>Implementation & timing ↗</h2><p>Control equations, architecture, loop responsibilities, and latency estimates.</p></a>
<a class="doc-card" href="docs/hardware.html"><span class="article-label">02 / CONNECT</span><h2>Hardware & wiring ↗</h2><p>Candidate parts, power domains, explicit jumpers, and integration constraints.</p></a>
<a class="doc-card" href="docs/build.html"><span class="article-label">03 / REPRODUCE</span><h2>Build & programming ↗</h2><p>Toolchains, CMSIS setup, FPGA implementation, and programming workflow.</p></a>
<a class="doc-card" href="docs/protocol.html"><span class="article-label">04 / COMMUNICATE</span><h2>Packet protocol ↗</h2><p>Command and telemetry layout, checksums, sequence validation, and faults.</p></a>
<a class="doc-card" href="docs/bringup.html"><span class="article-label">05 / COMMISSION</span><h2>Bench bring-up ↗</h2><p>Passive checks, current-limited experiments, timing captures, and output gates.</p></a>
<a class="doc-card" href="docs/calibration.html"><span class="article-label">06 / MEASURE</span><h2>Hall calibration ↗</h2><p>Reference gaps, current sweeps, model fitting, and independent holdout validation.</p></a>
</div>
```
